distractors.reason: We don't say 'back up strongly'. 'Strongly' describes force or firm belief, not the regular saving of files.
We don't say 'back up loudly'. 'Loudly' describes sound, so it does not fit this action.
We don't say 'back up highly'. 'Highly' describes a high level of quality or praise, not how often you save data.

example_sentence: You should back up your photos ___ on the cloud.
translation: hacer copias de seguridad con regularidad
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes a veces colocan el adverbio antes del verbo, diciendo 'regularly back up' en lugar de 'back up regularly'. En inglés el adverbio de modo va después del verbo.
explanation: In English, adverbs of manner or frequency that describe how often or how something is done usually come after the verb. 'Regularly' tells us how often the back-up happens, so it follows the phrasal verb.

related_collocations.example: This app saves your work automatically every minute.
Always log in securely when you use public Wi-Fi.
Charge your phone fully before the long trip.

memory_tip: Adverbs of manner and frequency usually come AFTER the verb: back up regularly, save automatically, log in securely
